mode: built-in image generation, one edit per option

options.name: White marble + satin champagne
options.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a faithful material variant of an existing interactive 3D portfolio website.
Input: The single supplied screenshot is the strict composition and geometry reference.
Change ONLY the surface materials of the winding ribbon and the surrounding frames/inset metal around the four existing colored glass portals. Preserve the exact camera, perspective, winding ribbon path, edge thickness, organic shapes, portal count, positions, sizes and floating air gaps. Preserve the four glass panes (sage upper-left leaf, warm beige central melted shape, pale blue angular right portal, pink/lavender lower-left hourglass), their color and reflectivity. Preserve the central faceted champagne tetrahedron exactly. Keep the existing cloud scene, daylight, shadows and open sky substantially unchanged.
The result must be plausibly implementable with PBR materials and texture maps on these exact meshes. No geometry changes, no new architecture or pedestal, no extra objects or frames. Do not invent theatrical lighting, subsurface glow, caustics, magical reflections, or volumetric effects. Maintain the same portrait aspect ratio and image bounds. Remove only the small black developer badge at the bottom left.
Design direction: exceptional but understated material craftsmanship, calm architectural quality, refined satin highlights, physically legible surfaces. Avoid plastic, excessive shine, decorative gold veins, dirt, conspicuous damage, grunge, glitter, bloom, blur, text, borders or labels. Material distinction must be clearly visible at this overview scale without exaggeration.
PALETTE 1 — WHITE MARBLE SPIRAL / SATIN CHAMPAGNE METAL FRAMES.
Create an unmistakable but understated contrast: the large spiral is neutral chalk-white honed marble, with sparse faint grey-beige mineral veins. Keep it bright neutral white, not yellow or cream. Change the ENTIRE broad outer frame surrounding every glass portal from white stone to solid SATIN CHAMPAGNE METAL: muted light yellow-gold, finely brushed, with gentle graduated metal highlights and a slightly darker champagne inset. The broad frame itself must visibly read as warm champagne all the way around, not merely a thin gold line inside an unchanged white frame. Gold is softly desaturated, not orange, gaudy brass, mirror-polished, or glittery. Preserve each exact existing thick organic frame profile and its beveled dimensions. Keep the tinted glass and central tetrahedron unchanged. Aim for quiet contemporary craftsmanship: cool-neutral pale stone ribbon contrasted with warm satin metal frames. Do not add veins to the metal or gold veins to the marble.
